about: BH3-03 (bug hunt 07.11.2026): ledger stamps after a backward wall-clock step. charge_clock(events, record, now, uptime, boot) -> the stamps budget() sees (pair_auto.py / lua/pair.lua). timelines: a failover charged at 'stamp'; 'same_boot' runs keep the RAM note (boot B, uptime start) and the wall clock is 'behind' seconds behind the stamp at the charge moment; 'other_boot' runs have no note and start at uptime 'start'. At t seconds later the next failover's cooldown spacing (max(cooldown,min_dwell) of the default settings, 60 s) must be met exactly when 'allowed'.

charge_clock.name: noted in this boot, clock unchanged: wall age wins (equal or larger)
noted in this boot, clock stepped back 3 h: monotonic age
noted in this boot, clock stepped back 30 s: monotonic age (inside the skew too)
noted in this boot, clock stepped forward: wall age wins (never longer than before)
a note of another boot is ignored: future beyond the skew counts as old as the uptime
no note, future beyond the skew: unknown age = uptime
no note, future within the skew: unchanged (budget clamps it to now as before)
no note, exactly CLOCK_SKEW in the future: unchanged
uptime earlier than the note (impossible in one boot): unchanged
mixed: one noted after the step, one old normal, one unknown future
damaged note rows are ignored (the stamp then has no note: unknown future = uptime)
invalid stamps pass unchanged (budget refuses them as before)

timelines.name: after a reboot, clock 3 h behind the stamp: at most one cooldown of uptime
after a reboot, clock 1 h behind the stamp
after a reboot, clock 30 s behind (inside CLOCK_SKEW): wall time as before, at most cooldown + 30 s
